title: A plea to leave arduous questions aside
source_text: LXXX. Caeterum tanta varietas sententiarum & opinionum circa naturam atque essentiam gratiae efficacis, & rationem ac modum quo in animis hominum operatur, quae a tot jam saeculis Scholas Christianas exercet, arguit rem esse perplexam, obscuram, & quae undique multis difficultatibus scatet: Nec spes est fore contentionum finem, nisi curiositati modus aliquis statuatur, & omittantur quaestiones arduae & non necessariae. Ac profecto longe consultius foret, & paci ac pietati Christianae conducibilius in totum ab ejusmodi quaestionibus abstinere, quam sine fine rixari de rebus, quae difficultate sua ingenium humanum obruunt, & in quibus vix quisquam sibi potest satisfacere.
pass_a_gloss: LXXX. Moreover so great a variety of opinions & views about the nature and essence of efficacious grace, & the reason and manner in which it works in the souls of men, which has now for so many centuries exercised the Christian Schools, shows that the matter is perplexed, obscure, & one that teems on every side with many difficulties: Nor is there hope that there will be an end of the disputes, unless some limit is set to curiosity, & arduous & unnecessary questions are left aside. And indeed it would be far more advisable, & more conducive to Christian peace and piety, to abstain wholly from questions of that kind, than to quarrel without end about things, which by their difficulty overwhelm the human mind, & in which scarcely anyone can satisfy himself.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXXX. The great variety of opinions and views on the nature and essence of efficacious grace, and on how it works in people's souls, which has occupied the Christian schools for so many centuries now, shows that the matter is tangled and obscure and full of difficulties on every side.

There is no hope that the disputes will end unless some limit is put to curiosity and hard, unnecessary questions are dropped. It would indeed be far wiser, and better for Christian peace and piety, to keep away from such questions altogether than to quarrel endlessly over matters that overwhelm the human mind by their difficulty and on which hardly anyone can satisfy himself.
